acceptance.must: Sprint validation accepts valid UTC boundaries and rejects empty names, inverted dates and invalid states; all new exports have direct tests.
Fixed header columns replace kind,payload; quoting, nulls, arrays, Unicode and all entity kinds round-trip; malformed or legacy rows have explicit behavior and failed imports preserve the store.
Plan groups ready tasks by project ID with existing readiness ordering, omits empty projects and excludes blocked or closed tasks.

Tabular CSV and JSON round-trip v2 sprints and membership; import replaces and validates sprint collections atomically. Version 0 and 1 stores migrate losslessly to v2 with empty sprints and null membership; both repositories validate sprint references, stable IDs and atomic rollback; existing stores remain readable.
Create/list/close use injected IDs and clocks, unique names, stable order and append-only events; repeated close is a conflict with no mutation.
A task belongs to at most one sprint; closed sprints reject assignment; unfinished members block closing; canceled/done members permit it; all changes are atomic and recorded.
Task queries and persisted views filter by sprint with deterministic ordering; invalid sprint references fail validation and import without mutation.
Inclusive UTC daily series uses activity and the injected clock; assignment, unassignment, cancellation and completion semantics are explicit and tested, including empty days and late events.
Commands expose create/list/close, assign/unassign, filtering and both new reports; help, parsing, stable JSON/table output and failure exit codes have direct tests.
Routes expose lifecycle, membership, filters and reports; request validation, error mapping, clock overrides and stable response contracts have direct tests.
Document CLI/API examples, v2 migration, sprint close rules, CSV columns/legacy handling and daily burndown semantics; examples match executable checks.
CLI and HTTP cover a complete sprint, v1 migration, saved views, plan and burndown, CSV/JSON round trips and failure rollback across process restarts; fast/full budgets remain satisfied.
